quizName: DMV Practice Test #14 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: At an uncontrolled intersection, what should happen if you and another vehicle arrive at the same time?

options.text: The vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlights to signal the other vehicle to go.
Keep going and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an intersection without signs or traffic lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: When should you keep more distance between you and the vehicle ahead?

options.text: When the road surface is slippery.
When traffic is light.
When you can see through vehicles ahead to check traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the road surface is slippery.
questions.explanation: You need extra space if your motorcycle takes longer to stop. This includes slippery pavement, blocked vision, or heavy traffic. Use at least a four-second following distance in these situations.

questions.question: What is the best way to help others see your motorcycle during normal riding?

options.text: Flash your lights.
Keep your high beam headlight on.
Paint your motorcycle a dark color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your high beam headlight on.
questions.explanation: The best way to make your motorcycle visible is to use your headlight and running lights. Use your high beam both day and night whenever it is legal and safe.

questions.question: If you carry a passenger on your motorcycle, what tire adjustment will you likely need to make?

options.text: Reduce tire pressure.
Make no changes to tire pressure.
Increase tire pressure.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase tire pressure.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight to your motorcycle, so you will need to increase tire pressure. Check your owner's manual for the correct pressure settings.

questions.question: In a group ride, where should inexperienced riders position themselves?

options.text: In the front.
Just behind the lead rider.
In the rear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the lead rider.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride near the front, just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch them from behind.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: On the left part of the lane, near the centerline.
On the right part of the lane, near the curb.
It depends on road and traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: The best lane position changes based on conditions. Choose the position that gives you the most visibility and space. Adjust your position as traffic changes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Right lane ends
Left lane ends
Traffic control device ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Right lane ends
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black lettering or symbols. This sign warns drivers that the right lane will end ahead.

questions.question: When following another vehicle, where should you position yourself?

options.text: Where the driver can see you in the side mirror.
Where the driver can see you in the rearview mirror.
Where the driver can see you through the passenger window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where the driver can see you in the rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Follow in the center of the lane behind the vehicle. This puts you in the driver's rearview mirror, which drivers check more often than side mirrors.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Ride on the shoulder of the road.
Decrease your following distance.
Increase your following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: At night, increase your following distance. Slow down and be ready to adjust your lane position.

questions.question: When other vehicles are slowed or stopped, what should a motorcyclist do?

options.text: Not weave between lanes of traffic.
Weave in and out of traffic lanes.
Ride in a straight line between two lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not weave between lanes of traffic.
questions.explanation: Do not ride between rows of stopped or slow vehicles. Vehicles may change lanes, doors may open, or arms may stick out. Motorcycles need the full width of a lane to stay safe.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: You must stop completely.
You may go through the intersection carefully.
You must let oncoming traffic go first.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop completely.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red traffic light. You must stop and wait for a green light before turning in that direction.

questions.question: When shifting gears during a turn:

options.text: Do it only if you can shift smoothly.
It is better than shifting before the turn.
It is the best way to control your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do it only if you can shift smoothly.
questions.explanation: It is best to shift gears before you start a turn. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly. A sudden power change to the rear wheel can cause your motorcycle to skid.

questions.question: On a motorcycle, which brake stops you the most?

options.text: The front brake
The rear brake
The emergency brake

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake
questions.explanation: The front brake provides about three-quarters of your motorcycle's stopping power. Use both brakes together every time you stop.

questions.question: When riding over grooved pavement in a work zone, you should:

options.text: Look down at the road surface.
Look ahead and keep your eyes up.
Move to the edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look ahead and keep your eyes up.
questions.explanation: Keep looking ahead through a work zone. Ride slowly over the grooved pavement.

questions.question: What is a difference between goggles and a windshield?

options.text: Goggles protect your eyes from wind, but a windshield does not.
A windshield protects your eyes from wind, but goggles do not.
A windshield keeps your eyes from watering better than goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Goggles protect your eyes from wind, but a windshield does not.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes from wind, but most windshields do not. A windshield is not a good substitute for goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, how does a motorcycle handle turns?

options.text: More slowly than usual.
More quickly than usual.
The same as usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: More slowly than usual.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight to your motorcycle. The extra weight means your motorcycle will respond to your movements more slowly. It will take longer to speed up, slow down, and turn.

questions.question: When riding in a group of motorcycles, where should inexperienced riders be?

options.text: Leading the group.
Near the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the front of the group.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride near the front of the group behind the leader. This way, experienced riders can lead and watch the less experienced riders at the same time.

questions.question: When it starts raining, where should you ride?

options.text: Off the road.
In the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
In the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the tire tracks left by other vehicles.
questions.explanation: When it rains, avoid the center of the lane. Instead, ride in the tire tracks left by cars in front of you. The left tire track is often best, but this depends on traffic and road conditions.

questions.question: If you have a passenger, which of these should you NOT do?

options.text: Ride slower than usual.
Leave more distance to stop.
Tell the passenger to hold onto the back of the bike.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the passenger to hold onto the back of the bike.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight and changes how your motorcycle handles. Ride slower and allow more stopping distance. A passenger should hold firmly onto the motorcycle's passenger grips or onto your waist and midsection—not just the back of the bike.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: You may exceed the speed limit until the pass is complete.
You may ignore no passing zone markings if you started in a passing zone.
You must follow the posted speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must follow the posted speed limit.
questions.explanation: All passes must be done at the posted speed limit and only in areas where passing is allowed.

questions.question: How are convex mirrors different from flat mirrors?

options.text: They show a narrower view of the road.
They show a wider view of the road.
They show a clearer view of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They show a wider view of the road.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors are used on many motorcycles. They show a wider view than flat mirrors. But they can make cars behind you look farther away than they really are.

questions.question: When entering a curve, where should you position your motorcycle?

options.text: On the left side of the lane.
In a position where you can see clearly and be seen clearly.
In the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: In a position where you can see clearly and be seen clearly.
questions.explanation: When entering a curve, change your lane position to see better and be seen better. Ride on the right side of your lane for left curves to see oncoming traffic early. Ride on the left-center for right curves to see oncoming cars without getting too close to the centerline.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The light is about to turn red.
The light is about to turn green.
Stop and wait for traffic to clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: The light is about to turn red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns that the light will turn red soon. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection when it turns yellow, keep going through.

questions.question: Before you start riding, make sure the fuel valve is:

options.text: Open.
Closed.
Covered.

questions.correctAnswerText: Open.
questions.explanation: Before you ride, open the fuel supply valve. If it is closed, the engine may start using old fuel in the lines, but it will stop running once that fuel is used up.

questions.question: How should you position your body on the motorcycle?

options.text: Use your arms to hold yourself up.
Use your arms to steer the motorcycle.
Stretch to reach the handgrips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your arms to steer the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Position yourself so your arms steer the motorcycle, not hold you up. Sit with your elbows slightly bent when you grip the handlebars.
